newsitem.title: USA: Acura looks for slight 1997 US sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Acura looks for slight 1997 US sales rise.

text.p: American Honda Motor Co Inc's Acura division said Wednesday it hopes to see slight sales increases in calendar 1997 in what is expected to be a flat U.S. luxury car market.
"Maybe 3,000-5,000, that would make me very happy," Richard Thomas, general manager of Acura, said following a presentation at the North American International Auto Show here.
Acura sold about 108,000 vehicles in the United States in calendar 1996.
Two new models should account for about 1,000 of those sales in 1997, the NSX sports car and Integra Type R sports coupe.

The NSX, priced at $84,000 for a special order hard top and $88,000 for the standard model, includes a 3.2 liter 290 horse power engine and six-speed manual transmission, Acura said. The car will go on sale next week.
The NSX is expected to sell 500-800 units in the 1997 model year, Thomas said.
The Integra Type R, with a 1.8-liter, 195 horse power engine, will be priced between $23,000 and $25,000 when it goes on sale in March and is expected to sell about 500 units, Thomas said.
American Honda is a unit of Honda Motor Co Ltd.
